chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'If a man commits fornication with his father's wife or his father's slave girl, that does not prohibit her to her husband, nor does it prohibit the slave girl to her master. That prohibition from him occurs only if he had intercourse with the slave girl while she was permissible (to him). Thus, that slave girl never becomes permissible to his father nor to his son. And if a man marries a woman with a valid marriage, the woman does not become permissible to his father nor to his son.'

key_terms.لِأَبِيهِ وَلَا لِابْنِهِ: to his father and to his son

ai.seo_question: Does fornication with a father's wife make her permanently forbidden to the son?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between *zawaj* (marriage) and *zina* (fornication) in establishing permanent prohibitions (*mahramiyyah*) for fathers and sons. It establishes that while valid marriage creates an eternal barrier, fornication only creates a permanent prohibition if the woman was originally permissible to the man committing the act, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that affinity is primarily established through contract rather than mere sexual union.
